root_cause.text: The `nduseroptmsg` struct's padding fields (`nduseropt_pad1`, `nduseropt_pad2`, `nduseropt_pad3`) were never initialized before being sent to userspace via netlink, allowing uninitialized kernel stack memory to be leaked to unprivileged users.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds three explicit zeroing assignments (`ndmsg->nduseropt_pad1 = 0; ndmsg->nduseropt_pad2 = 0; ndmsg->nduseropt_pad3 = 0;`) immediately after populating the other fields of the `nduseroptmsg` struct in the `ndisc_ra_useropt()` function. The CVE description explicitly states "The nduseroptmsg struct has three padding fields that are never zeroed and can leak kernel data," confirming that these padding fields were previously left uninitialized when the netlink message was constructed and transmitted to userspace.
